key_insight: GeSe can appear highly plastic in some loading paths yet fracture brittly in others, so plasticity in inorganic semiconductors must be judged across multiple orientations, scales, and deformation modes.
engineering_relevance: For flexible and curved-surface electronics, material selection should rely on a broader mechanical screening framework rather than a single compression test or crystal direction.
method: Bending along the c-axis armchair direction
evidence_signal: The abstract reports ~23% strain without fracture in macroscopic compression, but brittle cleavage in bending and fragmentation in conventional micropillar tests, with eccentric micropillar loading enabling interlayer sliding.
watch_item: A positive plasticity result from one specimen geometry or loading mode may not generalize because response depends strongly on orientation, sample size, and stress state.
paper_title: Identifying Plastic Inorganic Semiconductors Requires More Rigorous Criteria
